# D8_TRIGDEBUG_L7c368a4f: time_m_5 bars + trig_pullback_ema depth (len 10, w 0.5), Asia session of trading date 20261110 plus the 300 bars before it (W-D8SPEC, relay order 0037Z)

Documentation only. Series: ONE continuous series of all bars of row `time_m_5` (all sessions, 2023-04 to 2026-11-13, 256,215 bars, stored engine bars = the BASE set: time bars are unaffected by the print rule, see D8_PRINT_RULE.md section 5), sorted by session id then known time. Rows below: bar index 254811 to 255206; the Asia bars of 20261110 (sess 0, td 20261110) are idx 255111 to 255206 (96 bars, the last one truncated). I re-implemented the trigger loop in Python with every intermediate value logged and checked that my signals over the WHOLE series equal the module's `signal_fn` output exactly (64,064 signals; equal = True). 24 signals fall in this Asia session.

## Bar stamping and when a bar is known (code: `th_bars/build_month.py time_bars`)
- **time_m_5 is anchored on the first print of the session segment**, not on the epoch: bucket = floor((print time - first print of the session) / 300 s). In Asia the first print is at 18:00:00.000 ET = 23:00:00 UTC (verified on 98 of the last 100 Asia sessions), so bar boundaries are :00, :05, :10 ... of the UTC clock; a print exactly ON a boundary belongs to the NEW bar (floor). If a session's first print came late the whole grid shifts by that offset.
- **Known time = the bucket end exactly** (23:05:00, 23:10:00, ...) irrespective of any further print (unlike the tm<N> epoch bars, which wait for the next print). Column `known UTC` below. O = first print of the bucket, H/L = extremes, C = last print.
- **Empty buckets give no bar** (the bar index skips). **Session reset:** the bucket grid restarts at every session boundary (02:00, 08:30, 09:30, 12:00, 16:00, 18:00 ET) and at a contract change; the last bucket of a session is TRUNCATED: stamped at its last print (here 06:59:54 UTC), flag part = 1, and that bar gives no signal, but it stays in the series and enters the EMAs and ATR. 480 minutes of Asia = 96 five-minute bars on a normal day.
- **Contract roll:** bars never span a roll (segment break); the trigger code additionally back-adjusts older bars at an instrument change by the roll gap (column `roll adj`; 0 on all rows shown, the sample day has no roll).

## Indicator definitions (code: `triggers_b/core.py`, `impl_pb.py _pb_depth`, `registry.py`; all causal)
- **EMA(n)** = alpha*x + (1-alpha)*previous, alpha = 2/(n+1), **seeded with the first close of the whole series** (2023-04-03) and run over every bar of every session without reset. fast = EMA10(close), slow = EMA20(close) (slow = 2 x len). State carried into the first row below (idx 254811): EMA10 = 27177.883586, EMA20 = 27171.271245, ATR14 = 51.863454.
- **ATR14** = Wilder: ATR[i] = (ATR[i-1] x 13 + TR[i]) / 14, TR[i] = max(h-l, |h-c[i-1]|, |l-c[i-1]|) (TR[0] = h-l), seeded with the first TR, no reset (the previous close is the previous bar of the series, including the last bar of the previous session). The threshold uses the PREVIOUS bar's ATR: w x ATR14[i-1].
- **Trend:** up if EMA10 > EMA20, down if EMA10 < EMA20 (equal = keep the old state). When the trend becomes up (from not-up) the swing state is reset: swing high sh = h[i], pullback low pl = l[i]; when it becomes down: swing low sl = l[i], pullback high ph = h[i] (columns show the values USED at the decision, after this reset).
- **Long event (trend up, bar i >= 1):** (sh - pl) >= 0.5 x ATR14[i-1] AND close[i] > high[i-1]. Short mirror (trend down): (ph - sl) >= 0.5 x ATR14[i-1] AND close[i] < low[i-1], and i >= 2. After an event: sh = h[i], pl = l[i] (a new retrace must build up); without an event: if h[i] > sh then sh = h[i], pl = l[i]; else if l[i] < pl then pl = l[i] (mirror for down). Each qualifying bar is an event (no extra edge condition); bars with part = 1 and the first bar of the series give none.
- **Event time** = floor(known time to whole seconds) + 2 s (`ny_build.events`: `ts = t_ns // 10**9 + 2`); only events whose bar belongs to the Asia session (sess 0) are used.
- **Stop / target / flat time (events file columns, bracket plain60/60):** stop_pts = 60 and tgt_pts = 60 points from the entry fill, lots 1; exit_ts = the end of the signal's session = the next session boundary after the signal time: **02:00 ET = 07:00 UTC for an Asia signal** (the position is flat at session end); then the 120-second rule (`cap_exit`): if no print follows the scheduled exit within 120 s the exit is the last print before it. The entry is the engine's tape fill after the event time (set parameters fill 'through', hair 0.5, wait 10 s in the mf_multi stream; see D8_TRIGGER_DEFS.md / ENGINE docs); both sides are traded as engine-run (the L-id screen mode says long but the events file holds both).

## History NT8 must carry for every value to equal the engine's (plain paragraph)
The EMAs are seeded with the first close of the series (April 2023) and have no reset; the weight of the seed after N bars is (1-alpha)^N: for EMA20 (alpha 0.0952) 0.1% after 72 bars and 1e-6 after 140 bars, so any start more than about 150 five-minute bars (12.5 hours) back reproduces EMA10/EMA20 to 6 digits; the Wilder ATR14 (decay 13/14) needs about 400 bars (about 2 days of continuous 5-minute bars incl. all sessions) for 6 digits and about 150 bars for 3 digits. The pullback swing state (sh, pl, sl, ph) resets on every trend flip, so it needs only the last flip, normally within a few hours. NT8 must build the 5-minute bars exactly as the engine does: continuous across all sessions of the chart (including pre-open and NY sessions, which are bars of this series) with the grid re-anchored at each session boundary and a truncated last bar at session end, NOT NT8's own session-template minute bars across the 17:00-18:00 break. Practical rule: load ticks from the start of the previous trading day's Asia session (18:00 ET two days earlier) so that more than 400 bars precede the first Asia bar tested.
